tunables.label: Gateway Token
tunables.description: Bearer token that gateway clients must present; required in production when the gateway binds beyond loopback.
tunables.troubleshooting: Set a stable token (or OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PASSWORD) so clients survive restarts; a non-loopback bind with no auth path fails closed. The example is a local-only dummy value for compose validation.

tunables.label: Gateway Port
tunables.description: HTTP port the gateway listens on; must match the published container port.
tunables.troubleshooting: If the healthcheck times out, confirm the published mapping matches this value (18789:18789).

tunables.label: Node Environment
tunables.description: Node.js execution mode; the image already defaults to production.
tunables.troubleshooting: Leave at production — development mode enables verbose error pages and slower builds.

tunables.label: OpenAI API Key
tunables.description: OpenAI credential recognized by the core/bundled provider plugins when `models.providers.openai` is selected.
tunables.troubleshooting: Set it in the process environment or the trusted global dotenv at ~/.openclaw/.env — credentials read from a workspace `.env` are ignored by design. A 401 from api.openai.com means the key never reached the Gateway process.

tunables.label: Anthropic API Key
tunables.description: Anthropic credential for the `anthropic` provider (alternative to ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_TOKEN).
tunables.troubleshooting: If requests keep failing with 401 while the key looks right, check that it was not saved only in a workspace `.env`; use `openclaw doctor` to inspect effective provider config.

tunables.label: Gemini API Key
tunables.description: Google Gemini credential for the `gemini` provider (GOOGLE_API_KEY is also accepted).
tunables.troubleshooting: OpenClaw blocks GEMINI_API_KEY from workspace `.env` files; supply it via the Gateway process environment or ~/.openclaw/.env, otherwise the provider stays unauthenticated.

tunables.label: Groq API Key
tunables.description: Groq credential for the `groq` provider (fast open models).
tunables.troubleshooting: A 402/429 from Groq is an account or rate-limit issue, not a Gateway problem; confirm the key came from console.groq.com and lives in a trusted env source.

tunables.label: OpenRouter API Key
tunables.description: OpenRouter credential for the `openrouter` provider; useful as a single key across many models.
tunables.troubleshooting: Reference it from config as `${OPENROUTER_API_KEY}` only if the variable is present in the Gateway process env — an unset variable stays literal and logs a substitution warning.

tunables.label: DeepSeek API Key
tunables.troubleshooting: Provider keys cannot be redirected from a workspace `.env` (`*_BASE_URL` and `*_API_HOST` are blocked there too); set them in the process env or ~/.openclaw/.env.

tunables.label: Telegram Bot Token
tunables.description: Telegram bot token consumed when the Gateway is allowed to configure channels from ambient environment variables.
tunables.troubleshooting: Channels need an explicit `channels.` block in openclaw.json or the `--ambient-channels` startup flag — without one of them the token is ignored and Telegram never connects. Re-auth with `openclaw channels auth telegram` if the session expires.

tunables.label: Discord Bot Token
tunables.description: Discord bot token consumed when ambient channel auto-configuration is enabled.
tunables.troubleshooting: Same gate as Telegram: a `channels.discord` config block or `--ambient-channels` is required, and the bot needs the Message Content intent in the Discord Developer Portal.

tunables.label: Slack Bot Token
tunables.description: Slack bot token (`xoxb-...`) for the Slack channel adapter.
tunables.troubleshooting: Slack uses Socket Mode, so the matching app-level token (`xapp-...`) must also be configured in the `channels.slack` block; a token alone is not enough to connect.

tunables.label: Container Timezone
tunables.description: IANA timezone for the OpenClaw container, so logs, cron and session timestamps are not UTC.
tunables.troubleshooting: Use a zone installed in the image (for example `UTC`, `Asia/Jakarta`); an unknown zone silently falls back to UTC, which shifts scheduled jobs and log times.

tunables.label: Skip Onboarding
tunables.description: Bypasses the interactive onboarding/setup flow so the Gateway can start unattended (used by the upstream Docker setup scripts).
tunables.troubleshooting: Enable it for unattended container starts; leaving it off in a headless container can stall startup waiting for interactive input. Config still has to exist afterwards — the sample starts with `--allow-unconfigured` for that case.

tunables.label: Gateway Password
tunables.description: Password alternative to the bearer token for Gateway authentication (`gateway.auth.mode: password`).
tunables.troubleshooting: Pick either token or password auth — a non-loopback bind without one of them is rejected at startup. Treat it as a full-access operator credential; the example is a local-only placeholder for compose validation.

notes: The gateway starts managed via tini entrypoint (['tini', '-s', '--']). In Kubernetes, preserve entrypoint by passing arguments via args: ['node', 'openclaw.mjs', 'gateway', '--allow-unconfigured', '--bind', 'lan'] rather than overriding command. Explicit '--bind lan' is the sample solution to listen beyond loopback on container/Pod IP (config gateway.bind lan alternative supported); OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_BIND is not supported by runtime code. Runs as UID/GID 1000 (node:node); persistent volume mounted at /home/node/.openclaw requires writable ownership (fsGroup: 1000 grants group access if storage driver supports, not ownership universal guarantee). Probes are GET /healthz (liveness) and GET /startupz (readiness/onboarding reachability), both unauthenticated on the gateway port. Endpoint /readyz checks deeper operational state of configured subsystems; not proof provider inference; may be unsuitable for exposing onboarding if unavailable configured channel blocks. Gateway settings persist in ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json on the mounted volume, alongside sessions, state, and keys under ~/.openclaw. Provider keys and tokens are supplied via process environment or trusted global dotenv (~/.openclaw/.env) — never from a workspace .env.
